items.title: [Bounty Proposal] Qwen2.5-Coder (0.5B / 1.5B) Bring-Up using TTNN APIs
items.body:
### 📝 Background & Motivation

This bounty proposal is for bringing up the state-of-the-art compact code generation family **Qwen2.5-Coder** (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct` & `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct`) using **TTNN APIs** on Tenstorrent hardware (Wormhole and Blackhole).

`Qwen2.5-Coder` is currently the premier open-source lightweight coding LLM, achieving top-tier pass rates on HumanEval, MultiPL-E, and MBPP benchmarks at compact scales. Enabling native TTNN support for Qwen2.5-Coder provides Tenstorrent silicon users with high-throughput, low-latency, on-device code generation and reasoning.

---

### 🏗️ Architecture & TTNN Operator Mapping

The model follows a modern decoder-only transformer architecture with Grouped Query Attention (GQA), RoPE, SwiGLU MLP, and RMSNorm:

| Component | Standard PyTorch Equivalent | Native TTNN Operator Equivalent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Embeddings** | `nn.Embedding(vocab, dim)` | `ttnn.embedding` |
| **Pre-Attention / Pre-MLP Norm** | `Qwen2RMSNorm` | `ttnn.rms_norm` / `ttnn.rsqrt` |
| **Position Encoding** | Rotary Embeddings (RoPE, $\theta=10^6$) | `ttnn.transformer.apply_rotary_emb` |
| **Self-Attention** | Grouped Query Attention (14 Q / 2 KV heads) | `ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention` |
| **Feed-Forward Network** | SwiGLU (`gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj`) | `ttnn.linear`, `ttnn.silu`, `ttnn.multiply` |
| **Language Model Head** | `nn.Linear(dim, vocab)` | `ttnn.linear` / tied weights |

---

### 🧪 Acceptance & Validation Criteria

- [x] Full Python model architecture and weight loader for Qwen2.5-Coder.
- [x] Unit tests for `TTNN_RMSNorm`, `TTNN_RotaryEmbedding`, `TTNN_Qwen2_5Attention` (GQA), and `TTNN_Qwen2_5MLP` (SwiGLU).
- [x] End-to-end forward pass matching PyTorch reference outputs with Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) $\ge 0.99$.
- [x] Auto-regressive text and code generation demo loop.
- [x] Ready to be integrated into `models/demos/qwen/` in the `tt-metal` tree.

---

### 🙋 Contributor Status
I have implemented the complete architecture, verified unit test suites, and prepared the PR for integration into `tt-metal`. Looking forward to review and assignment!

items.title: Metal 2.0 port: data_movement/untilize — IdenticalNDShard factory (borrowed-DFB validator prerequisite)
items.body:
Port the remaining `UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputNDShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory` of `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/untilize` to Metal 2.0 / Host 2.0 APIs (Gen1 WH/BH target).

Parent: #41908
Follow-up to: #53583 (6 of 7 factories ported)

## Scope
Only the **input-and-output ND-shard-identical** factory of `UntilizeDeviceOperation`:
- `UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputNDShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory` (`device/factories/untilize_multi_core_input_and_output_nd_shard_type_and_shard_spec_identical_program_factory.cpp`)
  - kernels: `eltwise/unary/device/kernels/dataflow/reader_unary_sharded.cpp`, `data_movement/sharded/device/kernels/dataflow/writer_unary_sharded.cpp`, and `device/kernels/compute/untilize_variable_num_blocks.cpp` — all three already have `_metal2` forks created in #53583.

The other six factories are done (ported in #53583). The op runs mixed today — `select_program_factory` dispatches identical input+output ND-shard specs to this legacy `create_descriptor` factory, and per-factory dispatch keeps the op building and running. **This is the only remaining GREEN-subset factory.**

## Why this was deferred (blocker)
A faithful port — both input and output CBs are borrowed-memory (`CBDescriptor::buffer` set) → borrowed-memory DFBs via `DataflowBufferSpec::borrowed_from`, sized exactly as the legacy backed-CB `total_size` (`num_shards_per_core_in_group_1 × tile-padded-shard-tiles × tile_size`) — is rejected by the Metal 2.0 **spec validator** on **uneven ND sharding**.

`tt_metal/impl/metal2_host_api/program_spec.cpp:1567` enforces a *coarse* spec-time check `dfb_bytes <= tensor_spec.compute_packed_buffer_size_bytes()`, comparing the uniform per-node DFB size against the **whole logical packed tensor** size. For a heavily padded uneven shard the per-core DFB can exceed the whole logical tensor. Concrete failing case: tensor `[4,128,160]` bf16, shard `[3,96,96]`, 3-core grid → per-core DFB `3 shards × 27 tiles × 2048 = 165888 B` vs whole packed tensor `80 tiles × 2048 = 163840 B` — over by exactly one tile. The code comment there acknowledges this coarse check is imprecise for sharded tensors (the *precise* per-bank check runs later in `AttachBorrowedDFBBuffers`, `program_run_args.cpp`), but the coarse check is a hard `TT_FATAL`. **Even** ND-shard cases pass.

Failing test: `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/data_movement/test_untilize.py::test_untilize_nd_shard_to_same_shard_spec_uneven_input_shard_spec` (4 parametrizations).

## What needs to happen
1. **Metal 2.0 framework fix (prerequisite, separate track):** relax the spec-time coarse borrowed-DFB size check for L1-sharded `borrowed_from` TensorSpecs — defer wholly to the per-bank attach-time check in `AttachBorrowedDFBBuffers`, or compare against the sharded per-core allocation rather than the logical packed size. Owner: Metal 2.0 framework team.
2. **Re-audit + port** `UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputNDShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory` to `create_program_artifacts` (`ProgramSpecFactoryConcept`) once the framework fix lands. The conversion is otherwise mechanical (borrowed-memory DFBs via `borrowed_from`, named `dfb::`/`args::`, the `untilize_variable_num_blocks_metal2` fork already exists) — it was written and reverted during #53583, so the diff is known.

## Notes / instructions
- WH/BH only — no Quasar emulation.
- **Do NOT hand-tune the borrowed-DFB size to pass the coarse check** — buffer size is a correctness property in the tilize/untilize sharded family and hand-tuning it risks silent data corruption (cf. #51305).

items.body:
Port `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/untilize` to Metal 2.0 / Host 2.0 APIs (Gen1 WH/BH target).

Parent: #41908

## Scope
The six GREEN native `UntilizeDeviceOperation` program factories cleared for a mechanical port:
- `UntilizeSingleCoreProgramFactory`
- `UntilizeMultiCoreProgramFactory`
- `UntilizeMultiCoreNDShardInputProgramFactory`
- `UntilizeMultiCoreParallelizeColumnProgramFactory`
- `UntilizeMultiCoreSubCoreGridsProgramFactory`
- `UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory`

Deferred to a follow-up (see below): `UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputNDShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory`.

Out of scope (blocked pre-port): `UntilizeMultiCoreBlockProgramFactory` (per-node CB size, #51305) and the whole `UntilizeCodegenDeviceOperation` (no readiness-sheet row).

## Audit verdict: RED at op level; subset is clear
The pre-port audit cleared a GREEN subset of the native `UntilizeDeviceOperation` — `descriptor` concept, no custom `compute_program_hash`, no `get_dynamic_runtime_args` / `override_runtime_arguments`, no pybound `create_descriptor`, no offset-folded base pointers, all `TensorParameter` relaxations `none`, target `ProgramSpecFactoryConcept`. ## Status
Six factories ported and device-verified on blackhole. The `program_factory_t` variant is mixed (block factory + codegen stay legacy) and dispatches per-factory at runtime, so the op builds and runs:
- `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/data_movement/test_untilize.py` — 821 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed
- `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/base_functionality/test_tilize_untilize_2D.py` — 240 passed
- `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/base_functionality/test_untilize_bfloat8_b.py` — 176 passed
- `tests/ttnn/nightly/unit_tests/operations/data_movement/test_untilize.py` — 1 passed

`UntilizeMultiCoreInputAndOutputNDShardTypeAndShardSpecIdenticalProgramFactory` was deferred: the Metal 2.0 borrowed-DFB spec validator rejects the faithful uneven-ND-shard sizing (coarse spec-time `dfb_bytes <= whole-logical-tensor-bytes` check). Tracked separately.

## Notes
- WH/BH only — no Quasar emulation.
- Basic Metal 2.0 port (no functional changes expected). Five `_metal2` kernel forks created beside their legacy originals (+ two existing forks reused); untilize-only DM kernels converted in place; named `dfb::`/`args::` bindings, borrowed-memory DFBs, and per-group work-split multiplicity preserve legacy behavior.
- Reproduces (does not fix) a pre-existing latent cliff-writer RTA arg-count bug in `ParallelizeColumn` — flagged to the ops team, not touched in the port.

items.title: Metal 2.0 port: copy `SameMemoryConfig` factory blocked by `data_movement/move` reuse
items.body:
## Summary

The `SameMemoryConfig` program factory of `CopyDeviceOperation` (`ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/copy`) cannot be ported to the Metal 2.0 `ProgramSpecFactoryConcept` on its own, because the peer op `data_movement/move` reuses copy's factory **method** directly.

The op's other two factories — `DefaultRowMajor` and `DefaultTilized` — are ported (branch `gchoudhary/53550/metal2-data_movement/copy`, commit `91c23e7`). The framework dispatches ported and legacy factories per-factory at runtime, so the op builds and runs with `SameMemoryConfig` left on the legacy descriptor concept and the other two on Metal 2.0.

## The coupling

`MoveProgramFactory::create_descriptor` calls copy's factory method directly and returns its `ProgramDescriptor`:
- `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/move/device/move_program_factory.cpp:27` → `CopyDeviceOperation::SameMemoryConfig::create_descriptor(...)`

`MoveProgramFactory::override_runtime_arguments` then patches the buffer addresses at positional runtime-arg slot 0 of kernels 0 (reader) and 1 (writer), via `GetRuntimeArgs(program, 0/1)[...][0]`.

Porting `SameMemoryConfig` would:
1. Replace `create_descriptor` (returns `ProgramDescriptor`) with `create_program_artifacts` (returns `ProgramArtifacts`), which `MoveProgramFactory` cannot consume from its own `ProgramDescriptor`-based factory.
2. Move the buffer address off positional runtime-arg slot 0 (it becomes a `TensorBinding`), silently breaking `move`'s address-patching override.

A single factory struct cannot expose both `create_descriptor` and `create_program_artifacts` — that trips the `AllFactoriesValid` dual-concept `static_assert`.

## Proposed resolution

`data_movement/move` currently has a RED Metal 2.0 audit and cannot be ported easily yet. The most likely outcome is to **port copy's `SameMemoryConfig` factory simultaneously with `move`** when `move` is ported. At that point `move` either moves to Metal 2.0 (consuming a `ProgramArtifacts` / a Metal 2.0 `override_runtime_arguments`) or gets its own program-construction path, after which `SameMemoryConfig` ports cleanly.

## Notes for the eventual port

- Shared-pool kernels this factory will need forked (no `_metal2` forks exist yet): `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/kernel/dataflow/reader_unary_stick_layout_interleaved_start_id.cpp`, `.../writer_unary_stick_layout_interleaved_start_id.cpp`, `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/kernel/compute/eltwise_copy.cpp`, plus copy's four own same-memory kernels (`reader/writer_unary_start_id.cpp`, `reader/writer_unary_stick_start_id.cpp`).
- Audit process gap surfaced by this: the op audit's cross-check scanned only within the op directory; it should also grep tree-wide for external consumers of factory entry points, e.g. `grep -rn "SameMemoryConfig::create_descriptor"`.

Currently, our jobs have confusing names such as:
- Blaze - GLM MoE — Which GLM?
- Blaze - Chunked GLM (code_debug 55k) — Which GLM? Is this perf or accuracy test? How large is one chunk?

Introduce consistent naming:
- Remove `Blaze - *` from each job name as it holds no information considering (1) all jobs have it (2) CI is already called Blaze.
- Test that runs certain model should have (1) model name (Kimi, GLM etc.) (2) model version (Kimi-K2.6, Kimi-K2.7, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.1, GLM-5.2 etc.) (3) Model size (Kimi-K3-2.8T etc.). Kimi-K2.6 and Kimi-K2.7 come in 1T variant, while GLM-5.1 and GLM-5.2 come in 744B variant.
- Accuracy test should have `accuracy` tag. Similar to perf tests.
- All chunked tests (for example, `code_debug` 55k) should have chunk size included. That way, test will become `code_debug` 55k@5k.

items.title: [Dispatch]: DE firmware hangs when reading non-existent registers
items.body:
DE firmware hangs on some Quasar variants when reading from registers that aren't present on the DE:

* [`get_timestamp()`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/747b4f4a63efe5c21fd7af064d5fd43a55655d12/tt_metal/hw/inc/internal/tt-2xx/risc_common.h#L532-L543) uses registers only available on Tensix, but is called from [cq_dispatch_subordinate.cpp](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/747b4f4a63efe5c21fd7af064d5fd43a55655d12/tt_metal/impl/dispatch/kernels/cq_dispatch_subordinate.cpp#L456) (and possibly other locations).
* [`dispatch_dm.cc`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/f11e2083eef0991beb5c10201dbe7cd1e9f417f8/tt_metal/hw/firmware/src/tt-2xx/dispatch_dm.cc#L200-L202) queries the remapper to disable it, but the query can hang since the remapper doesn't exist on the DE.

These are the only instances of accesses to non-existent registers in the DE firmware that I've found, but there could be others.

items.body:
Port `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/copy` to Metal 2.0 / Host 2.0 APIs (Gen1 WH/BH target).

Parent: #41908

## Scope
All three `CopyDeviceOperation` program factories (one row per factory in the DFB/Metal 2.0 Porting sheet):
- `SameMemoryConfig`
- `DefaultRowMajor`
- `DefaultTilized`

## Audit verdict: GREEN
Pre-port audit cleared all three factories. `descriptor`-concept, no custom hash, no runtime-args update (`get_dynamic_runtime_args`), no `override_runtime_arguments`, no pybind descriptor, no offset-folded pointers, every `TensorAccessor` site 2-arg — a clean mechanical port to `ProgramSpecFactoryConcept`. Device 2.0 prerequisites satisfied for every referenced kernel (6 copy-owned + 6 donor/shared). No Appendix A feature in use (no GlobalCircularBuffer / `address_offset` / GlobalSemaphore).

Audit report: `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/copy/METAL2_PREPORT_AUDIT.md`

## Port work
- All tensor bindings (input + output) are Case 1 (via `TensorAccessor`) in every factory — bases are delivered as `Buffer*` runtime args today; mechanical `Buffer*` RTA → `TensorParameter` / `TensorBinding`, kernel builds `TensorAccessor(tensor::name)`.
- Self-loop the reader's scratchpad CB `c_0` in `DefaultRowMajor` (single toucher — reader both fills and drains it). All other CBs are legal 1:1.
- No RTA/CTA varargs — every kernel reads a fixed set of named args by constant index.
- Shared-kernel `_metal2` fork coupling:
  - `eltwise/unary` `reader_unary_interleaved_start_id` / `writer_unary_interleaved_start_id` — forks already exist, bind them.
  - `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/kernel/` pool `reader_/writer_unary_stick_layout_interleaved_start_id` and `compute/eltwise_copy` — no fork yet, this port creates the first (sunset lists: `embedding`, `concat`; `sharded_to_interleaved*`, `untilize_with_unpadding`).
  - `data_movement/sharded` `compute/eltwise_copy` — no fork yet (sunset list: `interleaved_to_sharded*`).

## Notes
- WH/BH only — no Quasar emulation.
- Basic Metal 2.0 port (no functional changes expected); style-fixup step deferred.
- One team-only anomaly noted in the audit: a dead CTA (`num_output_pages_in_row`) in `redistribute_pages_row_major_reader.cpp` — not porter work.

items.title: get_max_l1_space() misses HYBRID per-core allocations, so ttnn CB budgets can overestimate free L1
items.body:
## Summary

`ttnn::operations::data_movement::get_max_l1_space()` budgets CBs against `device->lowest_occupied_compute_l1_address()`, which in HYBRID allocator mode does not see per-core allocations on cores other than bank 0, nor any that live on a per-device rather than the mesh allocator. `ProgramImpl::validate_circular_buffer_region()` *does* see them. Ops budgeting with the helper can therefore build a CB plan the validator then rejects.

## Detail

The per-bank query is HYBRID-aware (`tt_metal/impl/allocator/allocator.cpp:425-439`): it also checks `AllocatorID{bank_id + 1}`, the bank's per-core allocator. But the device-level query only ever asks about bank 0, on the default sub-device manager's allocator:

```cpp
// tt_metal/impl/sub_device/sub_device_manager_tracker.cpp:160
constexpr uint32_t global_bank_id = 0;
const auto& global_allocator = default_sub_device_manager_->allocator(SubDeviceId{0});
auto found_addr = global_allocator->get_lowest_occupied_l1_address(global_bank_id);
```

The validator, in HYBRID mode, discards that value and walks every core in each CB's core range across every physical device allocator (`tt_metal/impl/program/program.cpp:1895-1911`), precisely because per-core allocations can land at different addresses per core and can live on per-device allocators.

So the two disagree in exactly the configuration per-core allocation exists to support: `experimental_set_per_core_allocation` on a core other than bank 0's.

## Affected callers

`get_max_l1_space()` / `is_enough_space()` in `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/data_movement/common/common.cpp:432`, reached from at least:

- `untilize` (native, via `enough_space_height`; and the codegen program factory as of #53399)
- `transpose`
- `matmul_utilities`
- `reshard_rm_program_factory`

Ops that place work over the full compute-with-storage grid are maximally exposed, since every core is in some CB's range.

## Suggested fix

Expose one frontier helper in the allocator layer that is allocator-mode-aware and takes a core range, and have both `validate_circular_buffer_region()` and the ttnn helpers call it. That removes the class of divergence rather than patching one caller.

Note the cost asymmetry when scheduling this: the precise frontier is an O(cores) walk. That is fine once per program-cache miss, which is where every current ttnn caller sits. It would not be fine on a per-dispatch path.

## Context

Raised as a suppressed comment in the Copilot review on #53399. Pre-existing — that PR tightens the codegen budget from whole-of-L1 to this helper's frontier, which is a strict improvement but inherits the blind spot.

Related: #53399

items.title: Cached programs' static CB region is never re-validated against live L1 on a cache hit
items.body:
## Summary

A program's statically allocated circular buffers are placed and validated exactly once, on the program-cache miss. On every subsequent cache hit the cached `Program` is reused with only its buffer addresses patched. If L1 occupancy has grown downward past the cached CB region end in the meantime, the CBs overlap the resident L1 buffer and corrupt it **silently** — the check that would have caught it does not run.

## Mechanism

`validate_circular_buffer_region()` is reached only through `compile_and_allocate()` (`tt_metal/impl/program/program.cpp:2662`) and `ConfigureDeviceWithProgram` (`tt_metal/impl/host_api/tt_metal.cpp:1059`). The ttnn cache-hit path reaches neither:

```
handle_mesh_adapter_cache_hit             ttnn/api/ttnn/device_operation.hpp:254
  -> validate_on_program_cache_hit/miss      (op-level validate, not CB placement)
  -> WorkloadFactory::apply_descriptor       (patches addresses only)
  -> enqueue_mesh_workload
```

Nothing invalidates the program cache when an L1 buffer is allocated — only `Device::close()` and an explicit `clear_program_cache()`.

## Repro sketch

1. Run an op on a shape whose CB region ends high in L1, with L1 otherwise free. This is a miss: the program is built and validated.
2. Allocate an interleaved-L1 tensor large enough that `lowest_occupied_compute_l1_address()` drops below that CB region end. Fill it with known data.
3. Re-run the identical op. This is a hit. No throw.
4. Read the L1 tensor back: contents are corrupted where the CBs overlapped.

Step 4 is the assertion that matters. Asserting only on the op's own output passes vacuously, because the output is typically not the memory that gets overwritten.

## Suggested fix

Cheap guard on the hit path: each `CircularBufferAllocator` already knows its region end, so cache the program-wide maximum at build time and compare it against `device->lowest_occupied_compute_l1_address()` on the hit. That is one allocator query plus one integer comparison per dispatch. Throwing the same diagnostic the miss path throws would already be a large improvement over silent corruption; forcing a rebuild would be better still.

If a per-dispatch allocator query is unacceptable on the hot path, gating the check behind the watcher/debug build would at least make the class of bug findable.

## Why this is worth fixing centrally

The hazard has two flavours and the second is spreading:

- Every op with static CBs has the weak form: the plan is a pure function of the cache key, but the frontier can still move underneath a cached entry.
- A growing number of ops have the strong form, where the plan itself is chosen from live L1 and so differs between the miss and later hits. Native untilize does this today via `UntilizeOperationAttributes::enough_space_height` (derived from `is_enough_space()` → `get_max_l1_space()`); `transpose`, `matmul_utilities` and `reshard_rm_program_factory` budget against the same helper.

Per-op mitigations exist — folding the live-L1-derived selector into the cache identity works, and native untilize effectively does it by accident since `enough_space_height` is an attribute and the default reflection hash includes it. But doing that op by op costs a per-dispatch allocator query each time and leaves the weak form unaddressed everywhere.

## Context

Surfaced by Copilot review on #53399, which fixes the miss-path version of this for `untilize_codegen`. That PR is monotone-safe with respect to this issue (the CB tier it selects is never larger than the whole-of-L1 tier `main` selects), so it narrows the window without closing it.

Related: #53399

Port `ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/moreh/moreh_nll_loss_unreduced_backward` to Metal 2.0 / Host 2.0 APIs (Gen1 WH/BH target).

Parent: #41908

## Scope

One `descriptor`-concept device operation, `MorehNllLossUnreducedBackwardDeviceOperation`, one program factory (2d/3d/4d are internal branches), four own kernels plus the `moreh_common.hpp` donor.

## Audit verdict: RED at op level; no portable subset

Every enumerated gate clears — Device 2.0, feature compatibility, factory concept, relaxation `none`, offset base pointers, `TensorAccessor` 3rd arg. The blocker sits outside the gate set: all three readers construct `DataflowBuffer` objects on `c_7`/`c_8`, which the factory never allocates, so no `dfb::` token exists to name and the kernels do not compile. Both fixes are functional changes the port may not make. One factory, tripped on every path, so no subset survives — no brief issued. Re-audit after the prerequisite merges.

## Notes

* WH/BH only; basic port, style fixup deferred.
* The blocker is also a live Blackhole bug: `read_line`'s scratch branch is taken at a 64-byte DRAM read alignment (32 on Wormhole, so masked there) and DMAs through an unconfigured CB's write pointer. Nightly is green because the value round-trips through that same address.
* `moreh_nll_loss_backward` allocates exactly these two; the omission here is the whole defect. That sibling has the inverse wart — a 2d `c_8` its reader never uses.
* **Separate ops-team items:** `compute_kernel_config` is vestigial yet hashed (no compute kernel, its one define unread), `writer_defines` is always empty, six `get_dataformat` locals are dead.

items.title: [Bug] Batch-1 Galaxy inference is broken on main
items.body:
Current tt-metal main cannot run the weight-free Llama 3.2 1B quick model test on a 32-device 8x4 Galaxy. The craq-sim Galaxy gate exposed three related no-prefetch decode configuration failures that had already been solved on the divergent nkapre/multichip branch but never reached main:

1. Fused-QK RoPE shards the already-doubled batch and rejects batch 1 because the position vector has two rows while the configured group has one.
2. After that is corrected, the QKV DRAM-sharded matmul requests in0_block_w=2 for a one-tile input shard.
3. The no-prefetch Galaxy LM head must shard vocabulary weights across both mesh axes and use interleaved DRAM matmuls.

A focused transplant of only those fixes onto current main is in PR #53513.

Related craq-sim PR: https://github.com/tenstorrent/craq-sim/pull/293
First failing run: https://github.com/tenstorrent/craq-sim/actions/runs/32128747183
Second failing run: https://github.com/tenstorrent/craq-sim/actions/runs/32134016180
